subject: Clarify: where requests are executed & subprocessor roster
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@trunovahealth.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@trunovahealth.com
Date: 2026-07-11T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: Data residency & subprocessors — initial questions

Connor —

Thanks for taking this. Before we get deeper into procurement, our security review needs a concise answer to where our data (requests and model execution artifacts) will be processed when we use Redwood's hosted API. Specific asks:

- Primary execution region(s) for the hosted (default) offering for US customers.
- Any known third-country hops (e.g., routing via EU/APAC) that could apply to requests originating in the US.
- List of subprocessors (compute/caching/logging/analytics) and their regions.
- Retention / deletion controls for request-level data and cache/KV. Are there APIs or contractual commitments to purge data on demand?

We'd like a short Q&A we can attach to our procurement docs. If you have a current subprocessor roster and a residency diagram, please attach.

Best,
Lydia Park
CISO, TruNova Health
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-11T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & subprocessors — initial questions

Hi Lydia —

Appreciate the clear list — summary answers up front, full details below and attached: redwood-subprocessors-2026.csv and redwood-residency-diagram-2026.png. Also attaching our SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf) per request.

High-level:
- Default hosted execution for US customers is in AWS us-east-1 (primary) with additional capacity in us-west-2 for regional failover.
- We do not route US-origin requests through EU or APAC under normal routing policies. Cross-border hops only occur if: (a) customer explicitly requests non-US region routing, or (b) a failure forces fallback to compatible regional capacity (rare—policy described below).
- Subprocessors: compute (AWS), model cache & KV (in-house service running on customer-region VMs), logging/analytics (Datadog in US), observability (Sentry, US), billing (Stripe/US). See attached CSV for full vendor list and regions.
- Retention & deletion: request logs and short-term artifacts are retained by default for 30 days; cached prefixes/KV have configurable TTLs. We provide API endpoints and a contractual DPA clause for on-demand deletion for both request logs and caches. Dedicated and Private deployments allow stricter residency/deletion SLAs.

If you need redlines to the DPA, or a statement of no cross-border transfers for a procurement clause, we can provide an addendum. Happy to do a short 30-minute call to walk through the diagram.

Next steps: tell me if you want the static subprocessor CSV or a sanitized version grouping 3rd-party names for procurement.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Lydia —

Following up with the engineering details you asked for. Below is a concise technical Q&A; I included routing/failover semantics and notes on cached KV.

1) APAC subprocessors during normal ops:
- No, for the hosted US tenancy we do not send request payloads to subprocessors in India or APAC for normal operations. Primary compute and all per-request processing remain in the customer region (AWS us-east-1 / us-west-2).
- We do run optional telemetry/analytics pipelines that aggregate anonymized metrics; those pipelines are configurable and can be restricted to US-only for customers with residency constraints. See subprocessor CSV for which observability vendors have APAC presence and opt-out instructions.

2) Region pinning / routing behavior:
- We support policy-based routing: customers can request region_pin = "us" which causes the platform router to only advertise capacity in US regions for that tenant. This is an automated, account-level setting (not a manual firefight).
- Failover: if all US capacity is exhausted/unavailable, the router will follow the configured fallback policy: either queue/return 503 (strict residency) or failover to nearest compatible region (if customer has allowed fallback). You can choose a strict residency setting in the Console or via API.

3) Cached KV and prefix locality:
- By default cached prefixes and KV entries are colocated with execution in the same region. TTLs and explicit cache-locality policies are configurable per-tenant. We expose an admin API to purge specific keys or flush prefixes; we can also perform contractual one-off purges if required.

Additional notes:
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) eliminate third-party subprocessors for compute and cache; only telemetry and optional support channels remain as external vendors if requested.
- Documentation & evidence: redwood-subprocessors-2026.csv (attached) lists each subprocessor, country of processing, and legal basis; redwood-residency-diagram-2026.png shows routing and failover hops.

If you want, we can produce an export that enumerates the exact regions for every vendor we use for your prospective tenancy (sanitized for vendor confidentiality). Happy to walk through with your engineering team this week.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
